classic-mixed-vegetables-canned-reduced-.title: Classic mixed vegetables, canned, reduced sodium, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Classic mixed vegetables (4782) are a blend of carrots, peas, corn, beans and other vegetables, cooked in oil with reduced sodium. The product is ready to eat, retains most of its vitamins and minerals, and offers a mild flavor and pleasant texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mixed vegetables are often used in quick meals because they are ready to serve.
Reduced sodium makes the product more suitable for people watching their salt intake.
Cooking in oil helps preserve aroma and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as A and K.
The product has a long shelf life without refrigeration.
The exact composition may vary by manufacturer but typically includes carrots, peas, corn, beans and sometimes sweet pepper.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The vegetables provide vitamin B6 and folate, which support metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Beta‑carotene and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Low sodium and the presence of potassium contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Improved vitamin absorption
items.content: Cooking in oil increases the bioavailability of fat‑soluble vitamins A and K.

items.title: Vegetable allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to specific components of the mix, such as peas or beans.

items.title: Oil content
items.content: The product contains oil, so those monitoring fat intake should consider its calories.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although reduced, the product still contains sodium; people with hypertension should monitor total salt consumption.

items.title: Can and preservative
items.content: After opening, the product should be stored properly to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mixed vegetables can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, soups, stews, pasta dishes, or used as a sandwich filling. They are also easy to heat in the microwave or on a skillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer the vegetables to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3‑5 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.

pasta-with-cream-sauce-seafood-and-added.title: Pasta with Cream Sauce, Seafood, and Added Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce, seafood, and added vegetables is a home recipe that combines a silky cream sauce, fresh seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari) and a mix of vegetables (bell pepper, zucchini, broccoli). The dish cooks quickly, is rich in protein, healthy fats and vitamins, and works well as a light dinner or a festive meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cream sauce is often made with heavy cream and Parmesan, giving the dish a velvety texture.
Seafood is a great source of omega‑3 fatty acids, which support heart and brain health.
Adding vegetables boosts fiber and antioxidant content, making the meal more balanced.
Pasta is traditionally cooked al dente so it retains a slight bite and absorbs the sauce better.
In Italy similar dishes are called “fettuccine alfredo with seafood,” but home cooks often use any pasta shape.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari) provides complete protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s from fish help reduce inflammation and support cardiovascular function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑grain pasta and seafood supply B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber and antioxidants
items.content: Vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini and broccoli add dietary fiber, vitamin C and polyphenols, aiding digestion and immunity.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: The cream sauce with Parmesan adds calcium, and fortified cream can contribute vitamin D, both beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels or calamari.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Cream and cheese increase saturated fat levels, so portion control is advised for those with heart disease.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared sauce and added seasonings can be salty; consider using low‑sodium broth or reducing added salt.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Seafood must be fresh and fully cooked to avoid bacterial contamination.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten; gluten‑free alternatives should be used for people with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, immediately after tossing it with the cream sauce, seafood and vegetables. Garnish with fresh parsley, grated Parmesan and a squeeze of lemon juice. The dish pairs well with a light white wine or sparkling water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. When reheating, add a splash of cream or water to restore the sauce’s creaminess. Freezing is not recommended, as the cream sauce may separate.

pizza-with-pepperoni-from-frozen-thick-c.title: Pizza with pepperoni, from frozen, thick crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with pepperoni is a ready‑to‑cook frozen product featuring a layer of tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and slices of spicy pepperoni sausage. The crust is thick and airy, providing a crunchy bite after baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pepperoni is an American version of Italian salami that became popular in the US in the 1950s.
Freezing preserves the flavor and texture of the ingredients for up to 12 months when stored properly.
Thick crust pizzas require longer baking times than thin crust but deliver a richer taste.
Pepperoni often contains higher sodium levels than regular sausage.
Pizza is commonly served with extra seasonings such as oregano or red‑pepper flakes.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Pepperoni and cheese provide a substantial amount of protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella is rich in calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sausage and dough contain vitamins B1, B2, and B6, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: The thick crust supplies complex carbohydrates that help maintain satiety.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomato sauce provides the antioxidant lycopene, which may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pepperoni is often high in salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and sausage are rich in saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑related conditions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The cheese makes this product unsuitable for individuals allergic to dairy proteins.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate
items.content: Some manufacturers add MSG for flavor enhancement; people sensitive to it should be cautious.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (392 °F). Place the pizza on a baking sheet or pizza stone and bake for 12‑15 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is fully melted. Let it rest briefly before slicing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen pizza at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After thawing (no more than 2 hours at room temperature) cook immediately. Do not store the cooked pizza in the refrigerator for more than 2 days.

content.title: About
content.content: 100% pomegranate juice is made from ripe pomegranates without added sugar, preservatives or flavorings. It has a vivid red color, a characteristic sweet‑tart taste and a rich aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The pomegranate is a symbol of fertility and abundance in many cultures.
Pomegranate juice contains over 200 bioactive compounds, including polyphenols and anthocyanins.
In ancient Egypt, pomegranates were used in rituals and as a longevity aid.
Pomegranate juice is widely used in Middle Eastern cuisine for marinades, sauces and desserts.
When not heat‑treated, the juice retains most of its vitamins and minerals.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols, anthocyanins and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Flavonoids improve endothelial function and may help lower blood pressure.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium aids fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and other phytochemicals strengthen the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to pomegranate.

items.title: High natural sugar content
items.content: Even without added sugar, the natural sugars can be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Pomegranate juice can increase the effect of certain medications, such as statins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice on its own, add it to smoothies, cocktails, sauces or marinades. For a milder taste, dilute with water or another fruit juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Freezing may cause crystallisation but the flavor remains intact.
